dataset.description: This dataset contains the source code files for the FPGA-based implementation of digital chaotic oscillators developed in the ChaoPower project. The oscillators are designed to replicate the dynamics of analog chaotic circuits and support robust synchronization with sensor nodes in a secure RF wireless power transmission (WPT) system. The code is written in VHDL/Verilog and targets low-power FPGA platforms. It includes modules for signal generation, control logic, and parameter configuration. The dataset enables reproducibility of the digital chaotic behavior and can serve as a foundation for secure embedded systems research.

distribution.title:
The purpose of the data collection and generation related to the FPGA-based chaotic oscillator design is to support the development, implementation, and validation of digital chaotic generators that replicate the dynamics of analog counterparts for secure wireless power transmission.

This data includes:

Simulation results validating the chaotic behavior of digital models;

Source code (VHDL/Verilog) for FPGA implementation;

Timing and logic analysis (e.g., power usage, synchronization time);

Experimental measurements from FPGA testbenches.

The data is critical for ensuring reproducibility, optimizing design parameters (e.g., robustness, resource usage), and demonstrating successful hybrid synchronization between FPGA-based digital oscillators (TX side) and analog oscillators (RX side). It also lays the groundwork for open-access dissemination and future reuse in chaos-based secure communication or power systems.

dataset.description:
Context
This dataset comprises results generated from numerical simulations and theoretical modelling related specifically to the RF Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system design. It focuses on modelling dynamically changing frequency hopping schemes and matching network optimization techniques essential for securely transmitting power using chaotic encryption methods. The models consider practical system parameters, frequency sensitivity, and RF energy transmission characteristics.

Purpose
The primary purpose of generating this data is to design, analyze, and optimize the secure wireless power transfer system proposed in the project. Specifically, it supports:

  • The development of optimal frequency hopping patterns based on chaotic oscillators to ensure security against unauthorized energy reception.
  • The optimization of matching network designs to achieve maximal power transfer efficiency under varying operating frequencies.
  • Validation of theoretical concepts for robust and secure RF power transfer.

These simulation and modelling outcomes directly contribute to achieving the project's research objectives related to secure, energy-efficient, and highly optimized RF wireless power transfer solutions.

distribution.title:
The modelling data is collected and generated to design and optimize the performance of a secure RF Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system based on chaotic encryption. The data supports the development of dynamic frequency hopping strategies and the optimization of impedance-matching networks at the receiver side to ensure selective, energy-efficient power delivery only to authorized sensor nodes.

This dataset contributes directly to achieving the following project objectives:

  • RO1: Design of low-power analogue chaotic generators for energy-efficient operation.

  • RO4: Integration of chaotic synchronization into a secure WPT system for selective power transmission.

Origin of the Data
The data originates from numerical modelling and simulation activities performed using specialized tools such as MATLAB, Simulink, and RF circuit simulation software (e.g., LTSpice, ANSYS HFSS). The models are based on theoretical formulations of chaotic signal behavior, matching circuit dynamics, and RF propagation properties. Simulations explore how frequency variations and circuit tuning affect energy delivery, efficiency, and system security.

dmp.description:
This Data Management Plan (DMP) outlines the principles, practices, and procedures for handling research data generated within the "ChaoPower – Chaotically Encrypted Wireless Power Transmission" project. The project aims to develop a secure, energy-efficient wireless power transfer system using hybrid analog-digital chaotic oscillator synchronization.

The DMP ensures that all data collected, processed, and generated throughout the project lifecycle complies with FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) data principles. It supports transparency, reproducibility, and long-term preservation of scientific results. The plan describes the types of data to be generated, metadata standards, data sharing practices, and strategies for secure storage, backup, and public dissemination via trusted repositories (e.g., Zenodo).

This DMP will be reviewed and updated periodically to reflect changes in data collection methods, publication strategies, or intellectual property considerations.
